title: Naturality as an affine automorphism action
exact_target: Which graphs admit an automorphism-compatible, simply transitive critical-group action on their spanning trees?
definition_tex:
\subsection{Definitions and mathematical statement}
Let $G=(V,E)$ be a finite connected loopless undirected graph, allowing parallel edges.
Its Laplacian acts on $f\in\mathbb Z^V$ by
$(\Delta f)(v)=\sum_{vw\in E}(f(v)-f(w))$, counting edge multiplicity.
Let $\operatorname{Div}^0(G)=\{a\in\mathbb Z^V:\sum_v a(v)=0\}$ and define the finite critical group
\[
 \operatorname{Jac}(G)=\operatorname{Div}^0(G)/\Delta\mathbb Z^V.
\]
Let $\mathcal T(G)$ be the set of spanning trees, with parallel edges treated as distinct choices.
An action of $\operatorname{Jac}(G)$ on $\mathcal T(G)$ is simply transitive if, for every $T,T'$, there is exactly one $a\in\operatorname{Jac}(G)$ with $a\cdot T=T'$.

Determine for which graphs there exists such an action that is equivariant under every graph automorphism:
\[
 \sigma(a\cdot T)=\sigma_*(a)\cdot\sigma(T)
 \quad(\sigma\in\operatorname{Aut}(G)).
\]
Here $\sigma_*$ is the automorphism induced by permuting divisor coordinates, and $\sigma(T)$ is the image tree, including the induced edge permutation.
This states precisely the minimum naturality requirement in the workshop.
The matrix-tree equality of the two cardinalities guarantees that arbitrary simply transitive actions can be transported along bijections, but such choices need not respect automorphisms.
The desired action should require neither a distinguished sink nor a cyclic ordering of edges around vertices.
The target is the existence and characterization of equivariant torsor structures, not merely a bijection between two finite sets of equal size.

\subsection{Short English statement}
Which graphs admit an automorphism-compatible, simply transitive critical-group action on their spanning trees?
